text:
Buffalo has handed Noah Ostlund a much bigger job, and he has taken it. He's playing 18:52 a night, up from 13:58 last season, and he's on the ice for 71% of the Sabres' power-play chances after 15% a year ago. His own chances have doubled, from 0.45 expected goals per 60 to 0.92.

The scoring hasn't caught up, and that's mostly luck. Buffalo has scored about six fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his shooting percentage (9.3%) sits under our range for him. Eleven points in 19 games could easily have been more.

He is a transition player through and through. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 67% of his shots coming off the rush last season and a carry-in on 54% of his entries, and a fifth of his setups going across the royal road. Joe Yerdon of Bleacher Report described one of those this week, a Jack Quinn feed that Ostlund turned into a 2-on-1 and a Zucker goal, as "a work of art on the rush."

Worth watching: he has gone two games without a shot. A breakout built on the rush needs him getting pucks to the net.
